channel.title: MidwestAEC™ — Building Science & Envelope Specifications
channel.description: Curated building science specifications, cold-climate envelope assemblies, and architectural trade engineering for Climate Zones 4 and 5.

item.title: Bathroom Fan Dripping Water? Why Exhaust Ducts Condense in a Cold Attic
item.description: Why bathroom exhaust fans drip in winter, how to tell condensation from a roof leak, and the DOE Building America guidance on duct type, insulation, slope, dampers and run time.

item.title: How to Pass a Blower Door Test on a Midwest Remodel: The Leaks to Seal First
item.description: What a blower door test measures, what the results mean for a Midwest home, and the ten leak spots to seal first on a remodel, from rim joists to attic hatches.

item.title: Does an Old House Need to Breathe? Air Leaks, Fresh Air and Why 'Build Tight, Ventilate Right' Wins
item.description: Does a house need to breathe? Why air leaking through walls and ceilings causes moisture damage and drafts in Midwest homes, and how sealing plus planned ventilation gives better air.

item.title: Vapor Barriers and Smart Vapor Retarders: What Midwest Walls Actually Need
item.description: Do Midwest walls need a plastic vapor barrier? How vapor moves both ways across the year, what Class I, II and III retarders are, when a smart retarder helps, and when exterior insulation replaces it.

item.title: Continuous Exterior Insulation: Why Foam on the Outside Keeps Midwest Walls Dry
item.description: Why continuous exterior insulation outperforms cavity insulation alone in Midwest walls: thermal bridging, warm sheathing, how much to use, and why re-siding is the time to add it.

item.title: Heating Bills Going Up? Where Midwest Homeowners Get the Most for Their Money
item.description: What Midwest households are expected to pay for heat this winter by fuel, why air leaks drive the bill, and the order of upgrades that pays back first, from air sealing to windows.

item.title: Standby Generators in a Midwest Winter: Sizing, Cold Starts and Carbon Monoxide
item.description: How to size a home generator for a Midwest winter outage based on your heating fuel, why cold weather makes generators hard to start, what cold-weather kits do, and CPSC carbon monoxide safety rules.

item.title: Insulating Under a Basement Slab and the Rim Joist: What to Use and Why It Matters
item.description: How to insulate under a basement slab and at the rim joist in a Midwest home: rigid foam and vapor retarder under new slabs, edge insulation, options for existing floors, and rim joist sealing.

item.title: When Replacing Windows Actually Makes Sense, and What to Ask For
item.description: When window replacement makes sense in a Midwest home, which ENERGY STAR and NFRC ratings to look for by climate zone, and the installation and flashing details to require in the contract.

item.title: Window Replacement Alternatives: How Low-E Storms and Air Sealing Compare
item.description: How low-E storm windows and air sealing compare with replacement windows in Midwest homes: field-measured heating savings, air leakage, cost, and when replacement still makes sense.

item.title: Basement Egress Windows: What It Takes to Cut One Into a Midwest Foundation
item.description: How basement egress windows work in Midwest homes: typical size requirements, cutting the foundation safely, structural support, silica dust control, and keeping the window well drained.

item.title: When the February Thaw Drips Through the Ceiling: Attic Frost, Ice Dams and Snowmelt in Midwest Homes
item.description: Water dripping from ceiling lights during a February thaw is usually melting attic frost, not a roof leak. How to tell the difference, why it happens in Midwest homes, and what to fix.

item.title: Why Are My Windows Wet Inside in Winter? Indoor Humidity, Cold Glass and What to Fix
item.description: What causes winter condensation on the inside of windows, the indoor humidity targets by outdoor temperature from Minnesota's Center for Energy and Environment, and when to fix the window instead of the air.

item.title: Rammed Earth in the Midwest: Thermal Mass, Freeze-Thaw and What Research Says It Takes
item.description: Can rammed earth walls and earthen floors work in the Midwest? Thermal mass vs. insulation, freeze-thaw durability, cement stabilization, and what HUD-published cold-climate research found.

item.title: SIPs vs. Stick Framing in the Midwest: What You Gain, What It Costs, and the Joint Detail That Matters Most
item.description: How structural insulated panels compare with 2x6 stick framing in Midwest homes: thermal bridging, airtightness, cost, and why sealing every panel joint matters, especially on roofs.

item.title: Insulation and Embodied Carbon: Comparing Spray Foam, Cellulose, Fiberglass and Mineral Wool
item.description: How common insulation types compare on embodied greenhouse gas emissions, why HFC-blown foams rank worst, where foam is still the right tool, and how to pick lower-carbon options in Midwest homes.

item.title: Rockwool vs. Fiberglass: How Each Holds Up in Midwest Walls
item.description: Mineral wool (Rockwool) vs. fiberglass batts in Midwest walls: R-value, fit, fire, sound, moisture and embodied carbon, and why air sealing matters more than which batt you choose.

item.title: Can a Heat Pump Handle a Midwest Winter? What Minnesota Field Data Shows
item.description: How cold-climate heat pumps perform in Midwest winters, using Minnesota field data: efficiency at low temperatures, how much heat they cover, backup heat, savings vs propane and electric heat.

item.title: High-Efficiency Furnace Shut Off in a Blizzard? Check the Vent Pipes Outside First
item.description: Why high-efficiency condensing furnaces shut down in snowstorms and extreme cold, how to safely check and clear the intake and exhaust pipes, and what DOE guidance says about vent placement.

item.title: Heat Pump Backup Heat Settings: Setting the Switchover Temperature So You Don't Pay for Strip Heat
item.description: Why heat pump bills spike when backup or auxiliary heat runs, what the switchover or lockout temperature does, and how to set it using Minnesota field data and your heat pump's specs.

item.title: Insulating Firebrick vs. Dense Firebrick: Which One for a Fireplace, Wood Stove, Pizza Oven or Forge
item.description: Insulating firebrick is light and blocks heat; dense firebrick is heavy and stores it. Which one belongs in a fireplace, wood stove, pizza oven, forge or kiln, with real numbers.

item.title: Mini-Split Frozen or Steaming Outside? Defrost Cycles, Snow and Ice in a Midwest Winter
item.description: Why ductless mini-split and heat pump outdoor units frost up in winter, how the defrost cycle works, what's not normal, and how cold-climate installation guidance says to place the unit for snow and meltwater.

item.title: Cold and Clammy: Why Your AC Leaves a Midwest House Humid, and How to Fix It
item.description: Why Midwest homes feel cold but clammy in summer, how oversized air conditioners fail to remove humidity, what humidity to aim for, and how to fix it with sizing, fan settings and dehumidifiers.

item.title: Attic Air Sealing and Baffles: A Step-by-Step Guide
item.description: How to air seal an attic step by step: pull back insulation, seal top plates, chases and lights, install eave baffles, seal the hatch, then add insulation, in the order UMN and BSC recommend.

item.title: Frost in the Attic: Why Midwest Roof Sheathing Sweats and Frosts in Winter, and How to Stop It
item.description: Why frost builds up on attic roof sheathing in Midwest winters, how to find the source, and why air sealing and controlling indoor humidity, not more vents, is the fix.

item.title: Ice Dam Leaking Right Now? Steaming vs. Chipping, and What to Do Today
item.description: What to do when an ice dam is leaking: rake the snow, open a drainage channel, hire low-pressure steam instead of chipping, and fix the attic air leaks that cause ice dams in the first place.

item.title: Midwest Ice Dams: Why They Form, What to Do Today, and Why a New Roof Rarely Fixes Them
item.description: Why ice dams form on Midwest roofs, what to do when one is leaking into your house, and why air sealing the attic, not a new roof or heat cables, is what prevents them.

item.title: Cold Upstairs, Ice Dams Outside: Air Sealing and Insulating Knee Walls in 1.5-Story Homes
item.description: How to air seal and insulate knee walls in 1.5-story Midwest homes: why the joist bays under the knee wall leak, the two DOE Building America approaches, and the order to do the work.

item.title: Roof Heat Cables for Ice Dams: When They Help, What They Cost, and the Fire Risk
item.description: Do roof and gutter heat cables stop ice dams? How they work, why they don't fix the cause, how to estimate the electricity, and CPSC fire safety rules for heat tape.

item.title: Insulating Over the Roof Deck: How to Fix a Cold Cathedral Ceiling When You Reroof
item.description: How adding rigid insulation over the roof sheathing during a reroof fixes cold cathedral ceilings and ice dams in the Midwest, and why at least 40 percent of the insulation should be outside the deck.

item.title: Barndominiums and Post-Frame Homes: How to Stop a Metal Roof From Sweating
item.description: Why barndominium and post-frame metal roofs and walls sweat and drip in Midwest winters, and how to insulate, air seal and control moisture so a metal building works as a home.

item.title: Keeping Pests Out of a Midwest Home: Gaps, Moisture and the Ground Around the House
item.description: How to keep mice, carpenter ants and termites out of a Midwest home by sealing gaps, fixing moisture and keeping soil, mulch and plants back from the house, with DOE and extension guidance.

item.title: Managing Water on a Midwest Acreage: Grading, Swales and Native Prairie Instead of Endless Mowing
item.description: How to manage runoff on a rural Midwest acreage: grading near the house, swales to carry water away, and native prairie that holds soil and cuts mowing, with DOE and Iowa State research.

item.title: Rural Backup Power, Propane and Batteries in a Midwest Winter: What Holds Up at Subzero
item.description: How propane tanks, lithium batteries, generators and well pumps perform in subzero Midwest winters, and how to plan backup power and fuel for a rural home, using industry and extension data.

item.title: No Water on a Frozen Morning? Well Pump, Pressure Tank and Pipe Freeze-Ups in Rural Midwest Homes
item.description: Why a private well loses water in a deep freeze, which parts freeze first, how to safely thaw them, and how to protect a pump house, pressure tank and pitless adapter.

item.title: How to Firestop and Air-Seal Balloon Framing Without Tearing Out Plaster
item.description: How to firestop and air-seal balloon framing in an older Midwest home: block the stud bays at the basement sill and the attic, seal the edges, then dense-pack the walls.

item.title: Balloon Framing: Why Older Midwest Two-Stories Are Drafty and How to Tell If Yours Is One
item.description: Balloon framing leaves the wall cavities open from basement to attic, which pulls cold air in and lets fire spread inside the walls. How to spot it and what the fix involves.

item.title: How to Insulate a Solid Brick Wall From the Inside Without Ruining It
item.description: How to insulate solid brick walls from the inside in an older Midwest home: fix rain control and mortar, test the brick, protect the joist ends, then use airtight insulation tight to the wall.

item.title: Should You Insulate an Old Brick House? Freeze-Thaw Damage, Joist Rot and What Research Recommends
item.description: Insulating a solid brick house from the inside makes the brick colder and wetter, which can lead to freeze-thaw damage and joist rot. What the research says and how to decide.

item.title: Why '100% Waterproof' Basement LVP Flooring Still Fails on Concrete
item.description: Waterproof vinyl plank can still buckle, smell or grow mold on a basement slab. Why moisture moves through concrete, how to test the slab, and what to put under the floor.

item.title: Why Water Comes Into Your Basement After Heavy Rain, and What Actually Fixes It
item.description: Why basements leak after heavy rain in the Midwest, where the water comes in, and which fixes work: grading, downspouts, drain tile and sump, and interior insulation that tolerates damp.

item.title: Frozen Septic Systems and Well Lines: Why They Freeze in Midwest Winters and What to Do
item.description: Why septic systems and private wells freeze in Midwest winters, how to prevent it with snow cover and mulch, and what to do and never do if yours freezes, from University of Minnesota and well industry guidance.

item.title: How to Encapsulate a Crawl Space: The Step-by-Step Conversion Guide
item.description: How to encapsulate a crawl space step by step: fix water, seal vents, lay and seal a ground vapor retarder, insulate walls with foam, seal the rim, dry the space and plan for radon.

item.title: Crawl Space Encapsulation vs. a Vented Crawl Space: Which Is Right for a Midwest Home
item.description: Sealed, insulated crawl spaces versus vented ones: why vents fail in Midwest summers and winters, what DOE research found on humidity and energy, and what encapsulation involves.

item.title: How to Know If You Need an ICF Basement: Signs, Options and When to Call an Engineer
item.description: Signs your basement has a problem, from white powder and musty smells to bowing walls, what each one means, which need a structural engineer, and when an ICF foundation makes sense.

item.title: ICF Basements: How Insulated Concrete Forms Perform in a Midwest Winter
item.description: How ICF basement walls perform in cold Midwest climates: R-value, air tightness, moisture, cost premium and payback, based on a DOE Building America cold-climate test house.

item.title: Spring Thaw Basement Flooding: Frozen Sump Discharge Lines and Battery Backups
item.description: Why sump pumps fail during the Midwest spring thaw, how to keep the discharge line from freezing, and how long a battery backup runs, using NDSU test numbers.

item.title: Frozen Sump Pump Discharge Line: How to Thaw It and Keep It From Freezing Again
item.description: Why sump pump discharge lines freeze in Midwest winters, how to safely thaw one, how freeze-relief fittings work, and where city guidance says the water should go.
